intro.title: A bar that arrives, and an evening that stays with people
intro.text1: Shake&Steer builds a complete cocktail bar inside your venue — the counter, the glassware, the ice, the garnishes and the people behind it. Everything is prepared in our own workshop and assembled on site hours before your first guest arrives.
intro.text2: We work with a short, seasonal list of house creations and a long book of classics, so every menu we write feels like it belongs to that one evening and to nobody else.
intro.imageAlt: Placeholder photo of a Shake&Steer bar set-up

events.moreText: Product launches, film wraps, gallery openings, private tastings. If there are people and a reason, we can build a bar for it.

process.title: Four steps from first message to last pour

s1.title: Talk it through
s1.text: Tell us the date, the place and roughly how many people. We reply with availability and a few honest questions.

s2.title: Design the menu
s2.text: We propose a menu built around your taste and your venue, including alcohol-free serves that nobody feels short-changed by.

s3.title: We set up
s3.text: The bar, ice, glassware, garnishes and team arrive early, install quietly and leave the space exactly as we found it.

s4.title: You celebrate
s4.text: You spend the evening with your guests. We take care of everything on the other side of the counter.

quote.text: They turned a corner of an old stone courtyard into the best bar in the city for one night. Half our guests are still asking for the recipe.

hero.title: Nine years of building bars in other people's rooms
hero.text: Shake&Steer began with one flight case, two bartenders and a stubborn idea: that a cocktail served at a private party should be every bit as good as one served in a great bar.

story.title: One flight case, one wedding, no plan B
story.text1: The first event was a friend's wedding in a courtyard with no running water and a single power socket. We built a bar out of borrowed crates, carried ice up two flights of stairs and served two hundred and forty drinks.
story.text2: Nothing about that night was easy, and everything about it was worth repeating. Since then the flight cases have multiplied, the bar has become a modular counter we designed ourselves, and the team has grown — but the working method has not changed. We turn up early, we prepare everything by hand, and we treat somebody's one important evening as exactly that.
story.text3: Today we pour at weddings in vineyards, birthdays in flats, product launches in galleries and christenings in family houses. The scale changes. The standard does not.
story.imageAlt: Placeholder photo from an early Shake&Steer event

values.title: Four things we refuse to compromise on

v1.title: Everything made from scratch
v1.text: Syrups, cordials, shrubs and infusions are produced in our own workshop in small batches, dated and tasted before they leave. No bottled sour mix has ever been on one of our trucks.

v2.title: Ice treated as an ingredient
v2.text: We cut our own clear blocks: large cubes for spirit-forward drinks, crushed for juleps, collins spears for highballs. Cold, slow dilution is half the reason a drink still tastes right at the bottom of the glass.

v3.title: A bar designed for the room
v3.text: Our counters are modular, and the front is dressed to suit the venue — oak, brushed brass, marble or draped linen. The bar should look like it was always meant to be there.

v4.title: Service you notice only when you need it
v4.text: Our bartenders are trained to read a room: quick and quiet during speeches, generous and warm on the dance floor, and never the loudest thing in the photographs.

craft.title: What your guests actually feel
craft.text1: A guest walks up to the bar and finds a short, legible menu — four or five drinks chosen for that evening, printed on good paper, with an alcohol-free option that reads as an equal, not an apology.
craft.text2: They are greeted by name if we know it, served in under ninety seconds, and handed a glass that is properly cold, properly balanced and beautiful enough to photograph. Then they go back to the party, which is the entire point.
craft.imageAlt: Placeholder photo of a cocktail being finished at the bar

team.title: A small core, and a bench we trust
team.text1: Every event is led by one of our senior bartenders, who is on site from the first crate to the last box. Around them we build a team sized to your guest list — typically one bartender for every fifty guests, plus a barback and a runner for larger evenings.
team.text2: Everybody who works a Shake&Steer bar has spent time in a real one. They arrive in uniform, they carry their own tools, and they know that the difference between a good evening and a great one is usually measured in small courtesies.
team.imageAlt: Placeholder photo of the Shake&Steer team

quote.text: We had planned a party and they delivered an evening. Three months later people are still talking about the drinks rather than the seating plan.

hero.title: Ten signatures, seventy ways to say yes
hero.text: These ten are the house creations we are known for. Behind them sits a full book of classics, spritzes, tiki serves and alcohol-free drinks — all of it in the PDF at the bottom of this page.

signature.title: The house list
signature.text: Rewritten twice a year around what is in season. Every one of them can be batched for large events without losing a thing.

c1.desc: Aged whisky softened with fig and vanilla, finished with a whisper of cherrywood smoke released at the table.

c2.desc: Gin stirred down with plum liqueur and golden chamomile, bright as a late-afternoon sun and twice as easy to finish.

c3.desc: Smoked mezcal, rose and pink grapefruit over a long block of clear ice — floral at the front, quietly smoky at the end.

c4.desc: Coastal gin, sea-salt tonic and a cordial of green olive and rosemary. Clean, saline and impossible to drink slowly in August.

c5.desc: Blackcurrant and burnt orange under a slow pour of champagne, served in a chilled flute with a single gold leaf.

c6.desc: Vodka washed with violet and blackberry, lengthened with sparkling wine and served the colour of the sky ten minutes after sunset.

c7.desc: Cucumber, green apple and lovage with a verjus cordial and soda. Every bit as considered as the drinks with spirits in them.

c8.desc: Dark rum, roasted pineapple and star anise, poured tall over crushed ice with a cinnamon-sugar rim.

c9.desc: Blanco tequila with blue butterfly pea, lime and a salted honey cordial that shifts colour as it dilutes.

c10.desc: Elderflower, white peach and champagne with a sugar cube soaked in bitters — our welcome drink of choice for weddings.

hero.title: A bar built around the evening you are planning
hero.text: Five kinds of event, three packages and a quote written for your date, your venue and your guest list. No fixed price list, because no two evenings are the same.

types.title: Five kinds of evening
types.text: Each one has its own rhythm. The list under every card is what a typical booking of that type includes.

weddings.title: Weddings
weddings.short: A signature couple's cocktail, a welcome pour for the aperitif hour and a bar that keeps the floor busy until the last song.
weddings.long: From the welcome pour as guests arrive to the last round after the band packs up. We coordinate directly with your planner, caterer and venue so the bar never becomes one more thing for you to manage.
weddings.i1: A signature cocktail created for the couple
weddings.i2: Welcome drinks and champagne service for toasts
weddings.i3: Printed menus matched to your stationery
weddings.i4: Site visit and timeline planning with your venue

private.title: Private parties
private.short: Rooftops, villas, gardens and apartments. We bring the bar, the ice and the music-friendly volume of service a good party needs.
private.long: House parties, rooftops, villas and garden evenings. A compact bar that fits through a normal doorway, a menu of four or five drinks, and a team that knows when to pour quickly and when to slow down.
private.i1: Compact modular bar for tight spaces
private.i2: Menu tailored to the host's taste

corporate.title: Corporate events
corporate.short: Launches, conferences and client evenings — branded serves, fast queues and an invoice your finance team will accept without a sigh.
corporate.long: Launches, conferences, staff parties and client evenings. We plan for peak demand — the fifteen minutes after a keynote ends — so nobody spends the networking hour in a queue.
corporate.i1: Branded serves, garnishes and menu cards
corporate.i4: Company invoice, insurance and licences in order

birthdays.title: Birthdays
birthdays.short: From a milestone dinner for twelve to a warehouse party for two hundred, built around the drinks the guest of honour actually likes.
birthdays.long: Milestone dinners, surprise parties and long nights in rented spaces. We build the list around what the guest of honour actually drinks, and keep one surprise back for the moment the cake arrives.
birthdays.i1: Menu built around the guest of honour
birthdays.i2: A birthday serve presented at the table
birthdays.i3: Flexible hours if the night runs long
birthdays.i4: Soft drinks and mocktails for every age

celebrations.title: Celebrations
celebrations.short: Christenings, anniversaries, engagements and homecomings — including gentle, alcohol-free menus for family gatherings.
celebrations.long: Christenings, anniversaries, engagements, graduations and homecomings — daytime events with mixed ages, where the alcohol-free half of the menu matters just as much as the rest.
celebrations.i1: Full alcohol-free menu, not an afterthought
celebrations.i3: Quiet set-up around a ceremony or service
celebrations.i4: Smaller bar footprint for family homes

other.title: Something else
other.long: Gallery openings, film wraps, product launches, private tastings, cocktail masterclasses for a team. If there are people and a reason to raise a glass, we can build a bar for it.

packages.title: Three starting points
packages.text: Think of these as a shape rather than a fixed offer. Every quote is written for your guest count, venue and hours — tell us what you need and we will adapt.
packages.footnote: Travel outside our standard service area, extra hours, additional bars and special licences are quoted separately and always agreed in advance.

p1.tagline: Intimate gatherings, up to about 50 guests
p1.i1: Modular bar, set up and taken down by us
p1.i2: Menu of four cocktails, one alcohol-free

p2.i2: Menu of six cocktails, two alcohol-free

p2.i6: Six hours of service, welcome pour included

a1.title: Welcome tray service
a1.text: Drinks carried to guests on trays as they arrive, so nobody has to find the bar before they have found their seat.

a2.title: Cocktail masterclass
a2.text: A 45-minute guided session for up to twenty guests — three drinks made, tasted and taken apart.

a3.title: Bottled gifts
a3.text: Your signature cocktail bottled, labelled and sealed as a favour for guests to take home.

a4.title: Late-night service
a4.text: A short, strong list for the last two hours: espresso serves, digestifs and one very cold beer.

faq.title: Questions we are asked most
faq.q1: How far in advance should we book?
faq.a1: For weddings in high season, six to twelve months is comfortable. Smaller parties are often possible with a few weeks' notice — always ask, because cancellations happen.
faq.a2: Usually yes, and it is included in the quote. If your venue requires you to supply the drink yourself, we are happy to work as a dry-hire bar instead.
faq.q3: What do you need from the venue?
faq.a3: A level space of roughly three by two metres, one standard power socket and access for loading. No running water needed — we bring our own.
faq.q4: How many guests can you serve?
faq.a4: We plan one bartender for every fifty guests. Above three hundred we normally suggest a second bar rather than a longer queue.
faq.a5: Yes. Travel within our standard service area is included; anything further is quoted openly, including accommodation where an early set-up requires it.

hero.text: Write or call — whichever suits you. We answer every enquiry personally, usually within two working days.

details.locationNote: Serving the whole region. Travel further afield quoted on request.

social.title: See what we poured last weekend
social.text: New menus, behind-the-bar preparation and pictures from recent events go up first on social. It is also the fastest way to send us a quick question.

info.title: Before you write
info.text: A first message with these five things lets us send back a real proposal instead of a list of questions.
info.i1: The date, or the two or three dates you are considering
info.i2: The venue, or at least the city and the kind of space
info.i3: Roughly how many guests you expect
info.i4: What kind of event it is, and how long the bar should run
info.i5: Anything that matters to you: a favourite drink, a theme, a budget range
